body:
## Motivation

Implements the check proposed by the maintainer in #3125 ("just raise an error"), which never
landed. Filed as #4534.

trtllm-gen fmha maps the batch dimension straight onto `gridDim.z`
(`numCtasZ = params.mBatchSize`). CUDA caps `gridDim.z` at 65535; beyond that,
`cuLaunchKernelEx` returns `CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE`, which `cuErrCheck` only prints to stderr.
The call then returns normally with the output buffer untouched — a **silent no-op** visible to
callers only as wrong results. A sentinel-filled-output micro-reproducer shows the exact onset:
batch 65535 writes output; 65536 leaves 100 % of the output untouched with no Python exception
(one stderr line). This is reachable in practice from sglang's DSA path, which flattens query
tokens into the batch dimension (sgl-project/sglang#34947).

## Modifications

One `FLASHINFER_CHECK(launch_config.gridDimZ <= 65535, ...)` immediately before
`cuLaunchKernelEx` (+13 lines), surfacing as a Python `RuntimeError` through the FFI. The comment
documents why only Z is guarded: gridDim.x carries Q tiles (limit 2^31−1), and gridDim.y
(head × head-dim splits) would need more than 2048 query heads to reach 65535.

Deliberately NOT changed: `cuErrCheck`'s print-only semantics (wide blast radius across the
trtllm tree) and the callers doing the flattening — the caller-side guard is
sgl-project/sglang#34948, and the structural cure for MLA prefill is the already-merged
`cum_seq_lens_q` path (#3238), which callers can adopt.

## Verification (B200)

| batch (= gridDim.z) | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 65535 | output written, no error | unchanged (output written, no error) |
| 65536 | output 100 % untouched, `exception=None`, 1 stderr line | `RuntimeError` naming the dimension, the value, and the remedy |
| 65536, unpatched control in the same env | silent | silent (proves the flip is this change) |

clang-format (pinned) clean.

## Related

- #3125 (this check), #3238 (structural cure for the MLA-prefill flattening)
- #4534 (issue tracking this guard; the print-only `cuErrCheck` half is deliberately
  left open there)
- sgl-project/sglang#34947 (end-to-end report), sgl-project/sglang#34948 (caller-side guard)
